subject: history_social
notes: Economist Priya Raman wanted to test whether a small discount encourages customers to bring their own reusable cups to cafés.
She worked with 20 cafés in Melbourne, Australia, that served drinks in disposable cups.
For three months, 10 of the cafés offered a 50-cent discount to customers who brought their own cup, and the other 10 did not.
At the cafés with the discount, the share of drinks served in customers' own cups rose from 4 percent to 11 percent; at the other cafés it stayed at about 4 percent.
stem: The student wants to present the method and the finding of Raman's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: For three months, 10 of the 20 Melbourne cafés in Raman's study offered a 50-cent discount to customers who brought their own cup, and the other 10 did not.
choices.B: Raman wanted to test whether a small discount encourages customers to bring their own reusable cups to cafés instead of using disposable ones.
choices.C: At the cafés in Raman's study that offered a discount, the share of drinks served in customers' own cups rose from 4 percent to 11 percent over three months.
choices.D: When 10 of 20 Melbourne cafés in Raman's study offered a 50-cent discount for customers' own cups, the share of drinks served in such cups rose from 4 to 11 percent there but stayed at about 4 percent elsewhere.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: how the study was done (the method) and what it showed (the finding). The key must describe the discount offered at half of the cafés and report the change in the share of drinks served in customers' own cups.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This gives the method only; it never says what happened as a result.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the aim of the study, which is neither its method nor its finding.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This gives the finding for the discount cafés but says nothing about how the study was set up, and it leaves out the comparison cafés.
explanation.D: Correct. "When 10 of 20 ... cafés offered a 50-cent discount" is the method, and the rise to 11 percent against a steady 4 percent is the finding.
